newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico rebels oppose train project in Oaxaca state.
newsitem.headline: Mexico rebels oppose train project in Oaxaca state.

text.p: Marxist Mexican rebels in the southern state of Oaxaca derided on Saturday a planned interoceanic railway there as just another way to make the rich richer, and called on local people to join their struggle.

The Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) said in a statement released on Saturday and dated Feb. 20 that the planned trans-Isthmus railway project -- part of the government's programme to privatise the national rail network -- "will be to benefit investors, while for our region it represents greater exploitation of natural resources and labour force, deepening the divide between rich and poor."

The EPR, which first appeared in southern Mexico in June last year and carried out attacks in several states in August, stopped short of threatening attacks on the planned rail link, which would provide transportation from the Gulf of Mexico to the Pacific Ocean.

The rebel group also said it was concentrating on propaganda rather than armed actions in its fight against the government of President Ernesto Zedillo. Its statement called on Oaxaca inhabitants to "join the ranks of the Popular Revolutionary Army... with the people's struggle, the EPR will triumph."

The EPR, which is also active in the southern state of Guerrero and has a presence in several other regions, said it carried out 20 propaganda operations in Oaxaca in January and February without clashing with goverment troops.
